input: Batch label and freeze summer berry portions

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing which types of berries are included changes prep steps — some need washing, hulling, or de-stemming before freezing.
Whether this is for one person, a family, or meal-prep for multiple people affects total quantity and portion sizing.
The intended use (smoothies, baking, snacking, etc.) determines whether berries should be frozen whole, sliced, or pre-mixed.
Available freezer space and container supply set hard limits on how many portions can realistically be done in one session.
The labeling method (masking tape, freezer labels, marker on bags) and container type (bags vs. rigid containers) shape the physical workflow.
Preferred portion size per unit directly determines how many individual portions to make and what size containers to use.
Knowing the target shelf life or how far ahead this should last determines freezing method and whether any pre-treatment like blanching or sugar-packing is needed.

gold.taskTitle: Batch label and freeze summer berry portions
gold.taskDescription: Prepare, portion, label, and freeze a batch of summer berries for later use.

questions.title: Which specific berry types are you freezing?
questions.description: Identify whether this involves strawberries, blueberries, raspberries, blackberries, or a mix, as each has different prep requirements before freezing.

questions.title: Who are these frozen portions being made for?
questions.description: Clarify whether this is for a single person, a household, or a larger group to determine total quantity needed.

questions.title: What will you mainly use these berries for later?
questions.description: Understand the end use — smoothies, baking, desserts, or snacking — to decide on whole vs. sliced and whether to mix berry types per portion.

questions.title: How much freezer space and how many containers do you have?
questions.description: Establish hard limits on batch size based on available freezer room and supply of bags or containers on hand.

questions.title: What containers and labeling materials are you planning to use?
questions.description: Determine whether you are using zip-lock bags, rigid freezer containers, or vacuum seal bags, and how you plan to label them (freezer tape, marker, printed labels).

questions.title: What portion size do you want per individual unit?
questions.description: Pin down the target weight or volume per portion (e.g., 1 cup, 200g) so the right number of containers can be prepared.

questions.title: How long do these portions need to keep in the freezer?
questions.description: Establish the target shelf life to decide whether any pre-treatment (sugar packing, flash freezing, blanching) is needed to maintain quality.
